title: Invoice edge cases: credits, overages, refunds, and proration for enterprise contracts
creator: Ava Chen
description: Clarify and implement deterministic behaviors for complex invoice scenarios that repeatedly surface in enterprise contracts: trial and promotional credits, commitment overage charges, mid-cycle plan changes (upgrade/downgrade proration), refunds for failed metering, and manual/automated adjustments. Goal is to reduce finance disputes, speed resolution time, and provide clear answers for security questionnaire items about billing accuracy and auditability.
problem_statement: Sales and Finance are seeing a growing number of enterprise disputes where the billed amount is unclear when multiple billing constructs interact (e.g., annual committed seats + monthly overage, trial credits applied, mid-term plan changes, and manual credit notes). These edge cases cause delays in procurement and trigger security/customer trust questions during RFPs and questionnaires.
proposed_solution: Define canonical rules for ordering operations on an invoice (credits -> subscription proration -> overages -> taxes), codify proration formulas for both monthly and annual commitments (day-based, timezone-aware), implement a billing reconciliation window and soft-lock for metering backfills, and surface a deterministic invoice explanation on the Console and in exported invoice metadata. Where automation cannot safely resolve (e.g., retroactive downgrade with disputed usage), expose manual adjustment workflows with audit logs and a JSON change record attached to invoices.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Documentation published in Confluence explaining how credits, proration, overages, and refunds are ordered and computed with worked examples for common combos (trial credit + upgrade mid-cycle; annual commit + monthly overage).
A2: Backend rule engine implements ordering with unit tests covering >95% of modeled enterprise scenarios listed in the spec.
A3: Console shows a line-by-line invoice explanation and a downloadable machine-readable invoice JSON with change history for every enterprise invoice.

A4: Billing reconciliation job identifies and queues metering anomalies for human review within 48 hours; auto-crediting applied only for safe classes (e.g., failed metering due to ingestion outage) and logged.
A5: Finance and Sales sign-off: two pilot enterprise customers accept the invoice breakdown for a test period reducing disputes by >=50% in pilot cohort.
A6: Security questionnaire answers updated to reference implemented audit trail and manual-adjustment controls (security review complete).
